mu-df74918e.stem: Which fibres of trapezius retract the scapula (towards the spine)?
options: None; trapezius does not retract the scapula
mu-df74918e.explanation: The middle fibres of trapezius retract the scapula. The upper fibres elevate it, the lower fibres depress it; upper and lower fibres together rotate it upwards.

mu-0d5e6a60.stem: What happens in the thoracic cavity when the diaphragm contracts?
options: The anteroposterior diameter of the chest decreases.
The ribs are pulled down and expiration occurs.
The dome rises and thoracic volume decreases.
The dome descends and the vertical diameter of the chest increases.
mu-0d5e6a60.explanation: When the diaphragm contracts its dome flattens and descends; the vertical diameter of the thoracic cavity increases and air flows in. Meanwhile intra-abdominal pressure rises.

mu-2efd9cbe.stem: What is the main action of serratus anterior?
options: Pulling the scapula forwards (protraction) and rotating it upwards
Depressing and pushing the scapula back
mu-2efd9cbe.explanation: Serratus anterior holds the scapula against the chest wall, pulls it forwards (the 'boxer's muscle') and, with trapezius, rotates it upwards so the arm can be raised above 90°.

mu-ae88dbac.explanation: The nerve to subclavius is a small branch of the upper trunk of the brachial plexus; it sometimes gives an accessory phrenic nerve that joins the phrenic nerve.

mu-366192ec.stem: What is the main function of transversus abdominis?
options: Compressing the abdominal wall to raise intra-abdominal pressure
mu-366192ec.explanation: With its horizontal fibres transversus abdominis tightens the abdominal wall like a belt; it raises intra-abdominal pressure in coughing, straining, childbirth and forced expiration, and stabilises the trunk.

mu-05477470.stem: Which is the main structure forming the anterior wall of the inguinal canal?
mu-05477470.explanation: The anterior wall of the inguinal canal is the external oblique aponeurosis (reinforced laterally by internal oblique fibres), the posterior wall the transversalis fascia (medially the conjoint tendon), and the floor the inguinal ligament.

mu-adf21325.stem: Which of the following is NOT a part of levator ani?
mu-adf21325.explanation: Levator ani consists of puborectalis, pubococcygeus (with pubovaginalis/puboprostaticus fibres) and iliococcygeus. Coccygeus is a separate muscle of the pelvic diaphragm.

mu-730ee30b.explanation: The axillary nerve supplies deltoid and teres minor. Supraspinatus and infraspinatus are supplied by the suprascapular nerve, subscapularis and teres major by the subscapular nerves.

mu-69780f6b.stem: What is the innervation of brachialis?
options: Mainly the musculocutaneous nerve (its lateral part also receives radial fibres)
mu-69780f6b.explanation: The three muscles of the anterior arm compartment (biceps, brachialis, coracobrachialis) are supplied by the musculocutaneous nerve; the lateral part of brachialis additionally receives fibres from the radial nerve.

mu-e17dab33.stem: What are the function and innervation of anconeus?
mu-e17dab33.explanation: Anconeus is a small muscle running from the lateral epicondyle to the lateral surface of the olecranon; it assists triceps and tenses the elbow joint capsule.

mu-36c5af6d.stem: What is the order of the superficial forearm flexors from lateral (radial) to medial (ulnar)?
options: Flexor carpi radialis, pronator teres, flexor carpi ulnaris, palmaris longus
Pronator teres, palmaris longus, flexor carpi radialis, flexor carpi ulnaris
Pronator teres, flexor carpi radialis, palmaris longus, flexor carpi ulnaris
Palmaris longus, flexor carpi radialis, pronator teres, flexor carpi ulnaris
Flexor carpi ulnaris, palmaris longus, flexor carpi radialis, pronator teres
mu-36c5af6d.explanation: Placing the right hand on the chest with the thumb lateral, you can count the four muscles: PT, FCR, PL, FCU. All arise from the common flexor origin on the medial epicondyle; FDS lies deep to them.

mu-6e2f450b.stem: Where do the FDS and FDP tendons insert in the fingers?
options: FDS on the middle phalanx, FDP on the distal phalanx
FDS on the distal phalanx, FDP on the middle phalanx
FDS on the metacarpal head, FDP on the middle phalanx
mu-6e2f450b.explanation: The FDS tendon splits in two at the level of the proximal phalanx (Camper's chiasm), and the FDP tendon passes through the split to reach the distal phalanx. DIP flexion is therefore produced only by FDP.

mu-c1a77b62.stem: Which muscle allows the index finger to be extended independently of the other fingers?
mu-c1a77b62.explanation: Extensor indicis is one of the deep forearm extensors and allows independent extension of the index finger (pointing). Its tendon is often used in tendon transfers.

mu-b5a54a42.stem: Mallet finger is an injury of which structure?
options: Collateral ligament of the MCP joint
Volar plate of the PIP joint
Terminal part of the extensor tendon inserting on the distal phalanx
Central slip of the extensor tendon
Insertion of the FDP tendon on the distal phalanx
mu-b5a54a42.explanation: A blow to the fingertip ruptures the end of the extensor tendon on the distal phalanx, and the patient cannot actively extend the DIP joint. A central slip injury causes a boutonnière deformity.

mu-73d28bd6.stem: What is the main action of piriformis?
mu-73d28bd6.explanation: Piriformis arises from the anterior surface of the sacrum, passes through the greater sciatic foramen and inserts on the greater trochanter; it laterally rotates the hip and abducts it when flexed.

mu-c21bde83.stem: What is the order of the deep lateral rotators of the hip from superior to inferior?
options: Obturator internus, piriformis, quadratus femoris, gemellus superior, gemellus inferior
Piriformis, obturator internus, gemellus superior, gemellus inferior, quadratus femoris
Quadratus femoris, gemellus inferior, obturator internus, gemellus superior, piriformis
Gemellus superior, piriformis, gemellus inferior, obturator internus, quadratus femoris
Piriformis, gemellus superior, obturator internus, gemellus inferior, quadratus femoris
mu-c21bde83.explanation: With gluteus maximus removed, from top to bottom one sees piriformis, gemellus superior, the obturator internus tendon, gemellus inferior and quadratus femoris; obturator externus lies deeper.

mu-3710da53.stem: What are the actions of sartorius?
options: Adducts and medially rotates the hip
Flexes, abducts and laterally rotates the hip; flexes the knee
Extends the hip and extends the knee
mu-3710da53.explanation: Sartorius performs all the movements of sitting cross-legged: hip flexion, abduction and lateral rotation, and knee flexion. It is supplied by the femoral nerve.

mu-488b8c00.stem: Which muscle forms the medial border of the femoral triangle?
mu-488b8c00.explanation: The femoral triangle is bounded above by the inguinal ligament, laterally by sartorius and medially by the medial border of adductor longus. Its floor is formed by iliopsoas, pectineus and adductor longus.

mu-0aeb820d.stem: Which spinal segment does the patellar (knee) reflex mainly test?
mu-0aeb820d.explanation: The patellar reflex runs through the femoral nerve and segments L2–L4, especially L4. The Achilles reflex tests S1, the biceps reflex C5 and the triceps reflex C7.
